DECISION AND ORDER OF THE ILLINOIS LABOR RELATIONS BOARD
STATE PANEL
On August 22, 2025, Executive Director Kimberly Stevens dismissed a charge filed by
Charging Party Latrice Moton on June 28, 2025. Charging Party was employed in the title
Veterans Certified Nursing Assistant by the State of Illinois, Department of Veteran’s Affairs
(“Employer”), and a member of the bargaining unit represented by Respondent American
Federation of State, County, and Municipal Employees, Council 31, (“AFSCME”). The charge
alleges that Respondent engaged in unfair labor practices within the meaning of Section 10(b) of
the Illinois Public Labor Relations Act (“Act”), 5 ILCS 315/1 et seq., by failing to file a grievance
challenging Charging Party’s transfer, her placement on administrative leave, and her termination
from employment. The charge also alleged that Respondent gave her conflicting information
about whether Chief Union Steward Genara Gordon would continue to help her in light of the
Charging Party’s filing of the instant charge.
The Executive Director dismissed the charge on grounds the allegations failed to raise
issues warranting a hearing. Noting the intentional misconduct standard in duty of fair
1

representation cases set forth in Section 10(b)(1) of the Act, the Executive Director observed
that Charging Party failed to provide evidence indicating Respondent took any action against her
due to any bias or hostility towards Charging Party’s activities and/or status that would constitute
intentional misconduct or that would undermine a union’s considerable discretion in contract
interpretation and grievance handling. She also found little evidence that Gordon’s alleged lack
of assistance hindered Respondent’s representation of Charging Party. Finally, the Executive
Director observed that Respondent did file a grievance over Charging Party’s discharge, which
was pending at the time of the investigation.
Charging Party timely appealed the Executive Director’s dismissal; the Respondent did
not file a response. On appeal, Charging Party claims the Executive Director failed to consider
evidence that Charging Party contends is key to demonstrating Respondent’s intentional
misconduct. Charging Party includes with her appeal text message exchanges between Charging
Party and Union Representative Tramkia Robinson, emails she sent to Robinson, and explains
how such evidence undermines the Executive Director’s determinations. She claims that the text
messages included as Exhibit A to the appeal demonstrate the Chief Union Steward’s “refusal to
assist due to the pending claim” and that the text messages included as Exhibit C to the appeal
demonstrate the Respondent’s inconsistency and neglect. Charging Party also asserts that her
email to Robinson contains a “Statement of Facts for Grievance, citing unlawful discrimination
and CBA violations.”
Upon review of the dismissal order, the record, and Charging Party’s appeal, we find the
appeal without merit for it offers no viable basis to undermine the Executive Director’s grounds
for dismissal. Specifically, the appeal fails to provide or point to any evidence that Respondent
failed to file or pursue a grievance for Charging Party due to any bias or hostility toward Charging
2

Party’s status or activity. Moreover, the materials included with the appeal fail to undermine the
Executive Director’s findings or raise issues for hearing on the elements of intentional misconduct
needed to prevail in duty of fair representation cases. Finally, as the Executive Director found,
Respondent did file a grievance over Charging Party’s discharge. Accordingly, the Executive
Director correctly dismissed the charge on grounds that the available evidence failed to raise issues
of fact or law warranting a hearing on the allegations that the Respondent engaged in unlawful
activity in violation of Section 10(b)(1) of the Act.
For the above reasons, we affirm the dismissal of the charge for the reasons stated by the
Executive Director.
BY THE STATE PANEL OF THE ILLINOIS LABOR RELATIONS BOARD
